author: Nayan Seth,Dewey Sim
description:
As American billionaires gathered at the White House to honour Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan last Thursday, a group of Chinese business leaders spent the evening on the sidelines.
They had travelled to the US capital to join the state dinner. But their invitations never arrived.
For weeks, their participation was the subject of intense discussion between Washington and Beijing.
While it was under consideration until the summit’s final hours, they were ultimately excluded...
title: Xi-Trump summit drew Chinese CEOs. So why couldn’t they get a seat at the table?

author: Vincent Chow
description:
US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday he does not want to work with China on addressing artificial intelligence (AI) risks, arguing that cooperation could undermine America’s lead in the fast-moving technology.
“Whoever wins superintelligence wins. You’re gonna have a winner and a loser, and you’re probably not gonna have a second place,” Trump said at the launch event for America.gov, a new AI-powered federal government portal.
“We’re leading now over China and everyone else, and I want to...
title: Trump rejects calls to work with China on AI safety despite Xi summit progress

author: Liu Zhen
description:
China has launched a rare air force support and training centre in Laos, the Ministry of Defence announced on Tuesday.
The China-Laos Joint Support and Training Centre and the China-Laos Friendship Aviation Academy are now in operation at the Ban Keun Airport, aiming to help the Laotian Air Force train its pilots, the ministry said in a statement.
The two institutions will be jointly maintained and operated by both sides, the statement said, without providing details on what personnel or...
title: China expands overseas military presence with new Laos air force centre

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
The US Navy has set up a dedicated command to turn its growing array of aerial, surface and underwater drones into an integrated fighting force – a capability US commanders have linked to disrupting a PLA attack on Taiwan.
The Robotic and Autonomous Systems Warfighting Development Centre, formally established on September 24 in Virginia, will develop doctrine and tactics for unmanned systems, train sailors to use them, and test whether they can keep operating under realistic conditions.
In a...
title: US Navy launches drone command that could reshape Taiwan war planning

author: Wang Wen
description:
For a decade, foreign policy circles have treated war between the United States and China as something close to destiny. The theory has a fancy, fashionable name borrowed from ancient Greece: the “Thucydides Trap” – the idea that a rising power and an established one are fated to collide, the way two articulated lorries merging into a single lane rarely ends well.
The term is widely used in commentaries on US-China relations. Frictions get written off as “inevitable” regardless of what actually...
title: What trap? US-China relations show conflict is far from inevitable

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
Beijing and Washington should first develop a common language around AI risks rather than seek to resolve their broader technology rivalry, a leading Chinese think tank has advised.
The call from the China Institutes of Contemporary International Relations (CICIR), affiliated with the Ministry of State Security, comes days after Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump agreed to formalise a new AI dialogue mechanism during their summit in Washington, their second such meeting...
title: US and China need shared risk vocabulary to manage AI threats: Beijing-linked think tank

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
Chinese researchers are drafting standards for autonomous satellite coordination and data sharing in a move analysts say could speed up military targeting and make People’s Liberation Army satellite networks more resilient.
An expert panel convened by the Chinese Institute of Command and Control (CICC) in Beijing on September 21 approved work on 10 proposed voluntary standards, clearing the way for draft texts to be released for consultation.
In an account of the meeting published last Thursday,...
title: Can China’s new satellite coordination standards boost PLA targeting and resilience?

author: Dannie Peng
description:
China is offering the world’s brightest young scientists generous 15-year research grants for free exploration, as the country accelerates its drive to become a global science powerhouse.
Dou Xiankang, director of the National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC), the country’s top funder of basic research, told a recent academic forum that the agency was selecting a group of the brightest researchers under 35 for long-term financial backing.
Once this group of exceptionally brilliant...
title: China offers 15-year research grants to the world’s brightest young scientists

author: Alyssa Chen
description:
China’s top diplomat Wang Yi met Japan’s former foreign minister Takeshi Iwaya, who is leading a 50-member delegation of corporate executives, in Beijing on Monday, marking the highest-ranking Chinese official reception for a Japanese visit in nearly a year.
During the talks, Wang warned that bilateral relations were facing a “severe situation” and had “yet to be normalised” ahead of next year’s 55th anniversary of diplomatic ties, according to a readout from the Chinese foreign ministry.
“A...
title: China warns Japan over WWII history as business delegation visits Beijing

author: Mark Magnier
description:
The US and China need to improve communication, work together more closely and more fully embrace technology to stem risks associated with artificial intelligence, the founder of Nvidia said on Monday.
“We should recognise that we’re competitors, and competitors are still able to collaborate,” said Jensen Huang, head of the world’s most valuable company, with a market capitalisation of about US$5.5 trillion.
“This is such an important and consequential technology. It has the incredible...
title: ‘Important and consequential’: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang on US-China AI race, risk management

author: Victoria Bela
description:
The ocean drilling ship Mengxiang has returned from its first expedition in the South China Sea, where it set a national depth record and obtained basalt core samples that could help to unravel the region’s tectonic history.
The 30-day expedition organised by the China Geological Survey tested the operational capabilities of the world’s most powerful deep-ocean drilling ship, according to a report published on Monday by the official ministry newspaper Science and Technology Daily.
During the...
title: Chinese deep-ocean drilling ship brings home ‘precious’ South China Sea samples

author: Liu Zhen
description:
China plans to complete a geological map of Mars by the end of 2028, as the red planet increasingly features in its space rivalry with the United States.
Hou Zengqian, chief scientist of China’s next Mars mission known as Tianwen-3, on Monday said the map would cover the entire surface of the planet and it aimed to be the global standard for the Martian geological ages.
State news agency Xinhua reported that the map would be the first AI-driven geological map of Mars and would be an important...
title: China reveals plan to map the entire surface of Mars by 2028 amid race with US

author: Daryl Ng
description:
The official opening of the Pinglu Canal on September 16 is a milestone in modern Chinese history. More than an infrastructural feat, it signals a strategic recalibration of how China’s inland economies connect with the sea and Southeast Asia, and augurs the next phase of regional growth.
Designed for vessels of up to 5,000 tonnes, the 134.2km (83.4 mile) waterway stretches from the Xijin reservoir in Hengzhou, an emerging city in Guangxi, to the Gulf of Tonkin (known as the Beibu Gulf in...
title: Hong Kong mustn’t miss the boat on the Pinglu Canal and Asean trade

author: Victoria Bela
description:
A Chinese team has set a world record for the most autonomous underwater drones operating at the same time, deploying more than a hundred of the small robots in a swimming pool test.
The Guinness World Record for “most autonomous underwater vehicles operating simultaneously” was set by a team from Northwestern Polytechnical University in collaboration with Xian Tianhe Maritime Technologies.
The trial involved a swarm of 116 autonomous underwater vehicles – called TH-618s, the university said in...
title: Chinese team sets world record with swarm of 116 underwater drones
